**suggestion (non-blocking):** The coaching batch can deny the whole roster after one student's lookup fails, so fall back per kaid on error.

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

One student's failed coach lookup can deny the whole roster. ManyCoachedBy on the coaches side (services/coaches/relationships/coachee.go:82-99) runs one getCoachCoacheePair per coachee in a tracegroup and g.Wait() returns the first error, so a single pair's datastore error fails the entire response. acl.ManyCoachedByActorErr then hands back an empty map plus that error (pkg/khan/acl/coaches.go:114-116), and this loader copies it into every slot at lines 39-46, which is where the line 40 comment ("The failure is not per-key") stops holding. isActorCoachOrAdminBatched logs the error and falls through to the admin check, so a teacher without progress-viewing admin gets Unauthorized for every row instead of just the broken one, where the unbatched isActorCoachOrAdmin failed per student. The sibling WcSession loader in this same PR takes the opposite tack and scopes a failure to the config that failed. Keep the successful batch path, and on error fall back per kaid with acl.IsCoachedByActorErr (the cached variable at pkg/khan/acl/coaches.go:36-40), retaining each result and error in its own slot. That adds calls only on the failure path and won't repair a service-wide outage. Reasonable to leave as is if you'd rather match services/progress/resolvers/coaching_loader.go, which does the same fan-out today.

</details>

```suggestion
if err != nil {
    out := make([]bool, len(kaids))
    errs := make([]error, len(kaids))
    for i, kaid := range kaids {
        out[i], errs[i] = acl.IsCoachedByActorErr(ktx, kaid)
    }
    return out, errs
}
```

**suggestion (non-blocking):** The new country-wide `crud.GetAll[models.District]` at line 1857 has no `.Limit()` and filters eligibility in memory; `is_test` and `roster_syncing_enabled` could move into the query, but `dont_send_kad_emails` is noindex.

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

This new `crud.GetAll[models.District]` at line 1857 has no `.Limit()`, so it loads every district with `country_code == countryCode` (the full entity, 61 `datastore:` properties, not a projection) and then discards the ineligible ones in memory at lines 1862-1874. Two of those predicates can move into the query: `IsTest` is `datastore:"is_test"` (district.go:114) and `RosterSyncingEnabled` is `datastore:"roster_syncing_enabled"` (district.go:143), both indexed. The third can't: `DontSendKADEmails` is `datastore:"dont_send_kad_emails,noindex"` (district.go:92), and `EligibleForKADEmails()` (district.go:451) is `SendKADEmails() && RosterSyncingEnabled`, so the opt-out half needs the noindex dropped and a backfill before it could be filtered server-side. To be clear this isn't a regression from the old path: the code removed here ran an unbounded `is_admin = true` GetAll over every admin UDI in datastore with no country filter, then `GetMulti` over the districts of all of them, so the district-side read is narrower now, and the comment at lines 1800-1804 shows the up-front-load tradeoff was already weighed. The only thing left is bounding growth of the new scan, either the two indexable equality filters (plus the matching index.yaml entry) or a `.Limit()` with a cursor. Non-blocking either way; is the district count per country small enough that you'd rather leave it unbounded?

</details>

```suggestion
Add `.FilterField("is_test", "=", testDistrictsOnly).FilterField("roster_syncing_enabled", "=", true)` to the query (with the matching index.yaml entry) and keep only the `SendKADEmails()` check in the in-memory loop.
```

**suggestion (non-blocking):** The country query loads every district before filtering, so page the read without dropping eligible recipients.

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

The new country-wide District read materializes ineligible entities before filtering, with no page bound. Page the country query with a limit and cursor, processing one page per invocation while retaining the eligibility checks. Do not silently truncate eligible recipients. DontSendKADEmails is stored with noindex, so adding index.yaml alone cannot enable that equality filter. Indexed is_test and roster_syncing_enabled filters can reduce the result set but do not bound its size.

</details>

**suggestion (non-blocking):** `errorToDebugMessage(err)` is passed a guaranteed-nil `err` in the phantom-user branch.

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

`errorToDebugMessage(err)` on line 180 is always passed a nil `err`. Control flow reaches line 175 only when `ktx.RequestUser()` on line 166 returned a nil error (the non-nil case returns at line 169), and `errorToDebugMessage` (line 157) short-circuits with `if err == nil { return nil }`. So every phantom/not-logged-in rejection returns `UNAUTHORIZED` with `debugMessage: null`, discarding the reason — while the `errors.Unauthorized()` constructed on line 176 for the log line is thrown away instead of being reused for the client-facing debug message. Introduced by this change; the four new tests all authenticate, so none covers this branch.

A sketch, not a committable replacement:

````
	if !acl.IsLoggedIn(ktx, acl.PhantomProhibited) {
		unauthorizedErr := errors.Unauthorized()
		ktx.Log().Warn(unauthorizedErr)
		return _mapErrorToAllClassrooms(
			graphql.WritingCoachConfigErrorCodeUnauthorized,
			&response,
			errorToDebugMessage(unauthorizedErr),
		), nil
	}
````

</details>

**suggestion (non-blocking):** The coaching batch can deny the whole roster after one student's lookup fails, so fall back per kaid on error.

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

Batching changes the failure blast radius on this permission check. services/coaches ManyCoachedBy (relationships/coachee.go:82-99) runs one getCoachCoacheePair per coachee in a tracegroup and g.Wait() returns an error if any single one fails, and acl.ManyCoachedByActorErr (pkg/khan/acl/coaches.go:114-116) then returns an empty map plus that error. This loader fans that error to every key, and isActorCoachOrAdminBatched logs it and falls through to actorIsProgressViewingAdminForUser, so one student's transient datastore error denies the whole roster for a teacher who isn't a progress-viewing admin. The upstream all-or-nothing behavior is pre-existing (services/progress/resolvers/coaching_loader.go:39-45 does the same fan-out today), but routing ai-guide's per-kaid check through the batch is new here, which is what turns a single-student failure into a roster-wide denial. Also, the comment on line 40 says the failure isn't per-key, and given that per-coachee loop upstream it often is. Worth noting the sibling loader in this same PR scopes errors per config for exactly this reason. So let's keep the successful batch path and, on batch failure, fall back per kaid with acl.IsCoachedByActorErr (the cached func var at pkg/khan/acl/coaches.go:36-40), retaining each result and error in its own slot. That adds calls only on the failure path and won't repair a service-wide outage (a RequestUser failure would just fail N times instead of once).

</details>

```suggestion
if err != nil {
    out := make([]bool, len(kaids))
    errs := make([]error, len(kaids))
    for i, kaid := range kaids {
        out[i], errs[i] = acl.IsCoachedByActorErr(ktx, kaid)
    }
    return out, errs
}
```

**suggestion (non-blocking):** getEmailableDistrictsByCountry loads every district with this country_code, full entities, no .Limit().

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

The new query at line 1855 filters only on country_code, and crud.GetAll at 1857 materializes whole District entities (61 datastore properties in services/districts/models/district.go), including the ineligible ones the loop at 1862-1874 then discards in memory. Nothing upstream bounds it: both callers (monthly_admin_email_batch.go:444, kad_email_subscriptions.go:529) pass a country code straight through, so the read scales with how many District entities exist in that country. Two caveats on the fix, so this is a suggestion rather than a must-do. Only part of the eligibility filter can move into the query: is_test and roster_syncing_enabled are indexed, but DontSendKADEmails is `datastore:"dont_send_kad_emails,noindex"` (district.go:92), so SendKADEmails() has to stay an in-memory check unless that property gets reindexed. And the code this replaced was itself an unbounded crud.GetAll over every is_admin UDI globally, so total reads probably go down here, it's just that the district kind now gets a country-wide scan. If you want it bounded, the cheap version is adding is_test and roster_syncing_enabled equality filters (plus the index.yaml entry) and keeping the SendKADEmails() check in the loop; the fuller version is .Limit() plus a cursor with one page per invocation.

</details>

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

One student's failed lookup denies the whole roster here. acl.ManyCoachedByActorErr wraps the coaches service's ManyCoachedBy, which runs a separate getCoachCoacheePair per coachee inside a tracegroup and returns a single error from g.Wait() if any one of them fails (services/coaches/relationships/coachee.go:82-99). So on the error path let's just fall back to acl.IsCoachedByActorErr per kaid (it's request-cached, coaches.go:36-40) and keep each result and error in its own slot, leaving the successful batch path alone. It won't repair a service-wide outage or a RequestUser failure, since those fail the fallback calls too. Note services/progress/resolvers/coaching_loader.go:39-45 already has this same fan-out, so this is a pattern question as much as a bug in the new file.

</details>

**suggestion (non-blocking):** `crud.GetAll[models.District]` here has no `.Limit()`, so the whole country's districts load as full entities before the in-memory eligibility filter; `is_test` and `roster_syncing_enabled` could move into the query, but `dont_send_kad_emails` is `noindex` so `EligibleForKADEmails` only partly pushes down.

<details><summary><sub>context</sub></summary>

`getEmailableDistrictsByCountry` runs `crud.GetAll[models.District]` at line 1857 with only a `country_code` equality filter and no `.Limit()`, so every district in the country is materialized as a full entity (61 `datastore:` properties in services/districts/models/district.go, no projection) and the eligibility filtering happens in memory at lines 1862-1874.

This isn't a straight regression though, and the prose in the original review overstated it: the pre-diff path did an unbounded `crud.GetAll[models.UserDistrictInfo]` over all `is_admin` UDIs in every country, so total read volume here probably went down, the unbounded read just moved to a wider entity kind and got scoped to one country.

Two of the three in-memory predicates are indexed and could move into the query: `is_test` (district.go:114) and `roster_syncing_enabled` (district.go:143), with a matching index.yaml entry. The third can't, `DontSendKADEmails` is `datastore:"dont_send_kad_emails,noindex"` (district.go:92), so `EligibleForKADEmails()` (district.go:451) can only be partly pushed down without a schema change and backfill. If the per-country district count is big enough to matter, paging with `.Limit()` plus a cursor is the option that actually bounds the read.

</details>
